environment.description: Application deployed identically but fronted by AWS CloudFront distribution with Lambda@Edge viewer-request function. The Lambda@Edge function implements a custom request normalization layer: it decodes all percent-encoded sequences in query string values, then applies a recursive token analysis that rejects any request where the decoded query string value contains a sequence matching the pattern of SQL syntax tokens (specifically: the function maintains a DFA that detects transitions between SQL keyword tokens like UNION/SELECT/FROM/WHERE/OR/AND followed by non-alphanumeric separators and subsequent identifiers, rejecting with 403 if the DFA reaches an accepting state). Additionally, the CloudFront distribution has a response header policy that strips any error detail fields from 5xx responses (preventing information disclosure from failed injection attempts). The origin is configured as a VPC origin with security group restricting inbound only from CloudFront managed prefix list, so direct access to the EC2 instance is not possible.

config.infrastructure: AWS EC2 t3.medium, Amazon Linux 2 (same AMI/code)
config.cdn: CloudFront distribution with custom origin (VPC origin via AWS PrivateLink)

lambda_edge.function_description: Query string normalization + DFA-based SQL token sequence detection
lambda_edge.coverage: all query string parameter values after full URL decoding (handles double-encoding, unicode normalization)
lambda_edge.detection_logic: Rejects if decoded value contains any SQL keyword token (case-insensitive) adjacent to operator characters or followed by identifier patterns

config.response_policy: Custom response headers policy strips 'detail' field from JSON error responses via CloudFront Functions on viewer-response
config.network_restriction: EC2 security group inbound: only from com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing prefix list on port 8080
config.waf: none (intentionally not using AWS WAF; protection is via Lambda@Edge custom logic)
